title: Database Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain what database performance contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: indexes.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. In this lesson, focus on indexes; then compare it with query optimization. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use database performance when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. For database performance, begin with indexes. Also distinguish query optimization; n+1 query avoidance; connection overhead. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.text: Know when to use indexes, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Query optimization
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
